scenarios.name: Checkout Regression
scenarios.description: Checkout form rendering regresses after a product is added to the cart while homepage, catalog, product detail, and basic cart access remain healthy.
scenarios.target_domain: Checkout page and checkout frontend flow
defect_behavior: After a product is added to the cart, the checkout form no longer renders the required checkout fields or actions.
Homepage, product listing, and basic cart access should remain unaffected.
A deterministic UI-level break is preferred over a crash or timing-sensitive service failure.
notes: Historical validation on 2026-06-11 used the then-current 50-test Playwright suite: 4 failed, 46 passed. The current canonical benchmark library has 51 tests.
Validated external scenario commit e5234240 against baseline commit 5096a85b.
Renaming only one label may make the signal too narrow.
Service crashes may broaden the signal through HTTP 500s or slow recovery.

scenarios.name: Cart Regression
scenarios.description: Adding a product to the cart fails deterministically, creating a cart-centered signal that also affects checkout and order flows dependent on cart state.
defect_behavior: Adding a product to the cart fails deterministically.
The preferred implementation is for AddItem to return a service error instead of storing the item.
Silent no-op behavior should be avoided because generic cart text assertions may still pass on an empty-cart page.
notes: Historical validation on 2026-06-11 used the then-current 50-test Playwright suite: 5 failed, 45 passed. The current canonical benchmark library has 51 tests.
Validated external scenario commit f7bac607 against baseline commit 5096a85b.
Only one direct cart assertion failed; several expected cart tests remained green, which indicates those tests are broad/soft and should not be treated as validated detecting tests.
A silent cart-state drop may not be detected by tests that only assert generic cart text.
A service error gives a clearer detection signal but may create frontend error-page assertions in multiple tests.
Checkout and order flows are expected to fail because they depend on cart state.

scenarios.name: Product Detail Regression
scenarios.description: Product detail lookup for valid product IDs fails or returns unusable data while homepage product listing remains intact.
scenarios.target_domain: Product catalog service and product detail pages
defect_behavior: Product detail lookup for valid product IDs fails or returns unusable product data.
Homepage product listing should remain intact.
The preferred implementation is to break GetProduct while leaving ListProducts healthy.
notes: Historical validation on 2026-06-11 used the then-current 50-test Playwright suite: 20 failed, 30 passed. The current canonical benchmark library has 51 tests.
External scenario commit 381043a6 on benchmark/scenario-ob003; baseline commit 5096a85b.
Failure scope is product detail and downstream flows depending on product detail.
Homepage/catalog listing remained sufficiently healthy because 30 tests passed.

scenarios.name: Payment Regression
scenarios.description: Valid Visa or Mastercard payments are rejected while cart, checkout form rendering, shipping quote, and product browsing remain healthy.
defect_behavior: paymentservice Charge always fails, so valid Visa or Mastercard payments are rejected.
Cart, checkout form rendering, shipping quote, and product browsing should remain healthy.
The preferred implementation is to reject otherwise valid cards after normal validation in charge.js.
notes: Validated against the full 51-test Playwright suite: 1 failed, 50 passed.
Baseline validation passed with 51 passed.
Failing test: payment-order-completion-confirms-success.
Validated external scenario commit b7ecc963 on benchmark/scenario-ob004.
Implementation changed src/paymentservice/charge.js so paymentservice Charge always fails.
This scenario intentionally has a narrow signal and depends heavily on a payment-aware successful order assertion.
Payment validation has date-sensitive logic, so tests should avoid relying on expiration edge cases.

scenarios.name: Currency Data Corruption
scenarios.description: Currency conversion data is corrupted so homepage price rendering fails under standard traffic while the code-change context points only at currencyservice data.
scenarios.target_domain: Currency service conversion and homepage price rendering
defect_behavior: The USD exchange rate is corrupted or zeroed in src/currencyservice/data/currency_conversion.json.
currencyservice conversion fails or returns invalid output for homepage price rendering.
frontend homepage rendering fails or returns an invalid page under standard traffic.
expected_runtime_effect: currencyservice error rate increases under standard traffic.
frontend error rate increases under standard traffic.
notes: OB-005 is the first runtime-aware scenario and uses the real committed Online Boutique file src/currencyservice/data/currency_conversion.json.
History + Code Change receives only the currency data changed-file context; it does not receive runtime metrics or oracle detecting tests.
The oracle uses direct homepage tests only.
QMind detection must come from runtime observability showing elevated currencyservice and frontend error rates, not from oracle leakage.

scenarios.name: Product Catalog ListProducts Cascades Into Homepage Rendering
scenarios.description: Product catalog ListProducts latency or failure is introduced in productcatalogservice code. Code change context points at productcatalogservice, while runtime observability shows the defect cascading into frontend homepage product-grid latency or rendering failure.
scenarios.target_domain: Product catalog listing dependency and frontend homepage product grid
defect_behavior: The productcatalogservice ListProducts path sleeps longer than the Playwright 30s test timeout or returns a deterministic gRPC error.
The productcatalogservice degradation is visible as elevated productcatalogservice latency and/or error rate under standard homepage traffic.
The frontend homepage path degrades because homepage rendering requires ListProducts before the product grid is built.
Cart, checkout, and payment tests that do not require product listing or homepage rendering should remain outside the direct oracle.
expected_runtime_effect: productcatalogservice p95 latency increases sharply or productcatalogservice error rate increases under standard traffic.
frontend p95 latency increases sharply and/or frontend homepage requests fail under the same traffic window.
scenarios.expected_user_visible_effect: Homepage load, homepage content checks, or product-grid checks fail due to the frontend-visible productcatalogservice cascade.
notes: OB-006 is the first combined-signal scenario: code change points to productcatalogservice ListProducts, while the direct oracle covers frontend-visible homepage, product-grid, catalog, and product-detail behavior.
History + Code Change receives only the productcatalogservice changed-file context; it does not receive runtime metrics or oracle detecting tests.
QMind detection must come from runtime observability showing both productcatalogservice degradation and frontend impact, not from oracle leakage.
Use runtime-scenarios/ob-006-productcatalog-listproducts-cascade/apply-ob006-productcatalog-listproducts.ps1 against an external Online Boutique checkout to inject or restore the defect.
